consensus_summary: Primary meaning is a place of divine presence, theophany/revelation, and God’s dwelling or kingdom (Sinai/Horeb, Zion, Transfiguration, etc.); common alternatives are earthly kingdoms/powers, faith-obstacles, stability, pride, or idolatrous high places.
book_summary: A kingdom, nation, or high place—the seat of ruling authority (opposite: valley).
consensus_core_identification: site of divine presence, revelation, and God’s kingdom/dwelling
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates the consensus alternative (kingdoms/powers) to the sole definition and adds ‘nation/high place’ as authority seats, while dropping or ignoring the dominant theophany/revelation cases (Sinai, Zion-as-dwelling, Transfiguration, etc.) that form the consensus primary.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary core (divine presence/revelation) cannot stand as the identification of the symbol if the book’s core (ruling authority) is accepted without remainder; the book replaces rather than qualifies the consensus primary.
rationale: Minimum cores differ in referent: presence/revelation vs. authority seat. Consensus already lists kingdoms as a common alternative and sometimes an extension of the primary, so the book’s cases are not absent; however, making authority the definitional core requires setting aside the settled primary identification and its paradigmatic passages. This is replacement of the central referent, not mere boundary adjustment around the same core, hence DIVERGENT with partial reclassification of the kingdom-related cases.
strongest_objection: The citations (Jer 51:25; Dan 2:35) support only the secondary kingdom reading and leave unexplained the large consensus body of theophany texts that the book’s definition does not cover.
